ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the radius of the semicircle is 5. The vertex of the $30^\circ$ angle of the triangle plate is placed on the semicircle, and the two sides of this angle intersect with the semicircle at points A and B, respectively. What is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
let point O be the center of the circle, connect $AO$, $BO$,\\
$\therefore$ $AO=BO=5$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOB=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=AO=BO=\boxed{5}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large semicircle, with the diameter on the horizontal line at the bottom, and the position of the center of the circle marked at the midpoint of the bottom; one vertex of a triangular board is placed at the right endpoint of the semicircular arc, denoted as C. The two sides emitted from this vertex intersect the semicircular arc at two points A and B respectively, A is on the upper-right arc, B is on the upper-left arc, and line segment AB is the chord connecting these two intersection points. The problem gives that the radius of the semicircle is 5, and the angle at vertex C is 30°. Reasoning: Let O be the center of the circle to which this semicircle belongs, and connect OA and OB. Because A and B are on the circle, and the radius is 5, OA=OB=5. Angle ACB is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is chord AB; the corresponding central angle AOB is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle, so ∠AOB=2×30°=60°. In triangle AOB, OA=OB=5, and the included angle ∠AOB=60°, therefore triangle AOB is an equilateral triangle. Thus AB=OA=OB=5.
